data.body:
Read **Feel the Buzz — Sound and Vibration** with a partner or use read-aloud. Explore **Key Words**, then play Matching and Memory. Use **Keep the Ideas Clear** as a reference. Try **Sort and Explain**, **Explain Your Thinking**, and **Check Your Understanding**. Use **Remember the Ideas** to build a memory cue. Read **Questions to Explore**, then complete **Try It with Evidence**.

Explain an answer using a detail from the lesson. Pictures support the activity text. A still picture cannot tell us exactly what a sound is like.

Picture panels: Feel and watch a shake; Different sounds; Join the investigation; Observe and record. Motion marks are drawing cues, not things you can see in the air.

history.title: Feel the Buzz — Sound and Vibration
history.data:
## Feel the Buzz

Put two fingers gently on your throat. Make a soft hum. Can you feel a buzz? Now stop. What changed?

A **sound** starts when something moves back and forth. To **vibrate** means to move this way. You may see the move. You may feel it. Some moves are too small to see.

Tap a **drum** gently. Its top shakes. That shake can make a sound. Touch the top to stop the shake. Listen for a change.

A **string** can shake too. A teacher can pluck one on a toy guitar. You can watch it move. When it stops, the sound fades.

A **loud** sound is strong to your ears. A **quiet** sound is soft to your ears. Loud is not the same as high. A small bell may have a high sound but still be quiet.

We use our **ears** to hear. We can also watch and feel safe objects. Do not put things in your ears.

We **test** an idea with a careful try. Tap the same drum gently. Listen. Stop its top with your hand. Listen again. Try more than once.

Sound can make other things shake too. A teacher can show thin paper moving near a speaker. Keep the sound at a safe level. What did you see?

data.question: Can I always see a shake?
data.answer: No. Some moves are tiny or very fast. You may hear or feel them.

data.question: Are loud and high the same?
data.answer: No. A sound can be high and quiet, or low and loud.

data.question: Must I hear to join the test?
data.answer: No. Watch the drum top or feel a safe surface with help. Share what you notice.

data.question: Can sound make paper move?
data.answer: Yes. A teacher can show this near a speaker. Use a safe sound level.
